clue.text: Leads to complaint, when servants go on a bender

definitions.text: Leads to complaint, when servants go on a bender

parts.words: Leads to complaint, when servants go on a bender
parts.note: domestic staff who spend all day kneeling to scrub floors develop a swelling of the joint named after them; 'go on a bender' is bending the knee, not drinking

explanation.surface: Servants go on a drinking spree and it ends in a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on a bender' suggests a drinking binge; here it means kneeling, which is how the inflammation of the kneecap's bursa got its nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the everyday name for prepatellar bursitis, an ailment caused by long kneeling.

clue.text: Futile to economise

explanation.surface: Trying to save money is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile means having no effect or purpose; to economise is to consume a smaller amount, read as two words.

clue.text: Sounds as if you, I and the French all used this sewing kit anyway

parts.note: et is the French word for 'and'

indicators.note: the word you is said aloud and heard as a single letter

parts.note: the pronoun spoken aloud is the letter U

explanation.surface: Everyone, you, I and the French, would use this little needlework case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds as if' turns the spoken 'you' into the letter U; 'all used this ... anyway' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles and other sewing items.

clue.text: In harmony about get ting older together

indicators.note: the two pieces are put together with one held inside the other

parts.note: growing older is ageing (the newspaper text splits 'getting')
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A couple grow old together in harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Together' looks like part of the growing-old picture, but it signals the container; 'get ting' is the newspaper's split of 'getting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of one mind and in accord is a synonym for consenting or concurring.

clue.text: A car to avoid

parts.note: a fairground bumper car whose name sounds like an instruction to evade them

explanation.surface: A warning about a vehicle you should steer clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: The name of the fairground car reads as 'dodge 'em', telling you to avoid the others.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the small electric bumper car of fairgrounds, named as if ordering drivers to evade one another.

clue.text: Japanese fight over hand cut meat

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: karate is a Japanese martial art
a chop is a cut of meat such as pork or lamb

explanation.surface: A Japanese bout ends with someone slicing meat by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand cut' sits in the middle of the clue: it is the definition, a blow with the side of the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A martial-arts strike with the edge of the palm is a blow that slices like a blade.

clue.text: Given no blessing from the heart to elevate the spirit

indicators.note: the answer is taken from inside the run of words, at their core

explanation.surface: Someone denied a blessing must lift their soul by sincere means.
explanation.definitionFit: To dignify or exalt in character is to raise someone morally.

clue.text: Splay out with leg speared horribly

indicators.note: horribly suggests the words are mangled into a new order

parts.note: the two words are the anagram fodder, with the A the setter meant restored

explanation.surface: A leg is gruesomely impaled and the limbs flop out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horribly' rearranges LEG SPEARED, but those ten letters lack the second A the grid needs: an A (perhaps 'with a leg') has dropped out of the clue as held.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread out the arms and legs wide is to sprawl in the shape of a heraldic bird.

clue.text: Steal pan and take chance there'll be something food in it?

definitions.text: there'll be something food in it?

parts.note: to take is to steal
a pot is a cooking pan
luck means chance or fortune

explanation.surface: A thief grabs a pan and hopes there is something tasty inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the hope there will be something good in the dish ('food' as held is likely a misreading of 'good'), which is what risking an unknown meal means.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means accepting whatever is available, originally whatever happened to be in the cooking vessel.

clue.text: The smart man takes his ale cold

indicators.note: the word takes signals that the answer is taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A clever fellow likes his beer chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: A smart alec is a know-all; the letters sit across 'ale cold'.
explanation.definitionFit: The name completes the idiom 'smart alec', a cocky know-all.

clue.text: Hateful to belt a steed that's run off-course

indicators.note: a horse straying from the course suggests letters thrown out of order

explanation.surface: It is cruel to whip a horse that has bolted from the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hateful is loathsome, deserving intense dislike.

clue.text: Normal, but not general, way to get a seat

definitions.text: Normal, but not general, way to get a seat

parts.words: Normal, but not general, way to get a seat
parts.note: a seat in Parliament won at a poll held between nationwide votes, not at a general one

explanation.surface: A remark on the usual way of finding somewhere to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat' suggests a chair; it is a parliamentary seat, filled by a vote in one constituency when not at a general poll.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a poll in a single constituency to fill a vacancy between national votes.

clue.text: Trying to write a composition

explanation.surface: Making an attempt at writing a school piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay is to attempt, so the participle means attempting; it is also writing a short literary piece.

clue.text: The right kind of floor for a long passage

explanation.surface: Choosing suitable flooring for a lengthy corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: A levelled layer of cement laid on a floor, and also a long tedious piece of writing.

clue.text: Unpunctuality makes Sal tense

indicators.note: the letters given make something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: Being late puts Sal on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to arrive on time is tardiness.

clue.text: By word of mouth, or on a friend's say-so

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Something passed on by speech, or on a pal's assurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Done by speech, spoken rather than written.

clue.text: A town and/or a state with a king in Europe

parts.note: the conjunction is taken as written without its slash
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A town or nation in Europe ruled by a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Andorra is a small principality in the Pyrenees between France and Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a tiny sovereign principality in the Pyrenees.

clue.text: A broad view of Panama, or its interior

indicators.note: the second word is put into the inside of the first

parts.note: the Central American country, taken as written

explanation.surface: A sweeping scene of Panama, or of its inland regions.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide unbroken vista over a whole area.

clue.text: Fungus as life-threatening as a tiger, we hear

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken and the letters entered follow its sound

parts.note: a tiger can be a man-eater, a beast that kills people, preceded by 'a'

explanation.surface: A poisonous mushroom said to be as deadly as a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'a man-eater' gives the name of the deadly mushroom genus that includes the death cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus of mushrooms, many highly toxic, including the death cap.

clue.text: Prohibit use of force if backed up within the island

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the other word

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit
F is the physics abbreviation for force

indicators.note: the word if is read backwards

explanation.surface: Banning force on a remote isle if it is supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use of' is a link; 'the island' is Baffin Island in the Canadian Arctic, so the definition is a proper name.
explanation.definitionFit: A large Arctic landmass in northern Canada, the fifth largest on Earth.

clue.text: A woman and man go together to the Spanish section of church

parts.note: a lady is a woman
a chap is a man
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A couple go together to the Spanish part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel dedicated to the Virgin Mary within a larger church.

clue.text: Shopping centre in smart London street

explanation.surface: A shopping centre on a fashionable street in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mall is the grand avenue leading to Buckingham Palace in London.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed shopping precinct, and the ceremonial avenue running up to Buckingham Palace.

clue.text: Film star reaches her peak at the side of her man

indicators.note: the star's surname is split so that one part stands beside the other, and that part is dropped

parts.note: Ingrid Bergman, the Swedish film actress
her man is a man, the word itself

explanation.surface: An actress reaches the top beside her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The film star is Ingrid Bergman: take away the 'man' at the side and the peak is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain, as in the Afrikaans word for one, or the iceberg's tip.

clue.text: Toy dog

explanation.surface: A small breed of dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Corgi is a well-known British brand of die-cast model cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand of die-cast model vehicles, and a short-legged Welsh herding breed favoured by the late Queen.

clue.text: In contrast to the Lorelei, these sirens are dangerous to ignore

definitions.text: In contrast to the Lorelei, these sirens are dangerous to ignore

parts.words: In contrast to the Lorelei, these sirens are dangerous to ignore
parts.note: the Lorelei siren lured sailors to ruin by being heeded; alarm sirens bring danger only when not heeded

explanation.surface: Unlike the legendary river siren, these calls must be heeded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sirens' suggests the mythical temptresses; here they are alarms.
explanation.definitionFit: Alerts that something hazardous is imminent, such as alarms or flashing lights.
